The queried nodes ann, bob and eve are outlined. For the pair ann, bob both parents are lowest common ancestors (accent color, with their four edges); ann and eve share no ancestor. The card maps (ann, bob) to mum and dad and keeps (ann, eve) with an empty list." width="100%"} Applies `all_lowest_common_ancestors()` to many pairs at once, sharing the ancestor searches between pairs. Use it to find all the most specific shared categories of many pairs of terms in an ontology with multiple inheritance, or every merge base of many pairs of commits. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pairs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of `(u, v)` pairs (IDs or labels). If `None` (default), every pair of nodes, including each node with itself. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[tuple[int, int], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(u, v)` to the IDs of its lowest common ancestors, in ID order, for every pair. Unlike in `all_pairs_lowest_common_ancestor()`, a pair without a common ancestor is kept, with an empty list. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not a directed acyclic graph, is empty, or a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each node's ancestor set is computed once and cached; each pair then costs an intersection and a scan of the common ancestors' successors. This follows `all_pairs_all_lowest_common_ancestors` from NetworkX pull request #7988. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#6da05069 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec family = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["mum", "dad", "ann", "bob", "eve"]) family.add_edges([("mum", "ann"), ("mum", "bob"), ("dad", "ann"), ("dad", "bob")]) label = family.get_label_from_id found = family.all_pairs_all_lowest_common_ancestors([("ann", "bob"), ("ann", "eve")]) {tuple(label(n) for n in pair): [label(a) for a in lcas] for pair, lcas in found.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {('ann', 'bob'): ['mum', 'dad'], ('ann', 'eve'): []} ``` ::: :::
